editorial:
Set in the gritty streets of Istanbul, this Turkish drama follows Mehmet, a sick waste warehouse worker who spends his days sorting through trash. When he finds a small boy named Ali hiding in the garbage, he takes the child in and tries to give him a better life. The film has a raw, emotional feel that pulls you into Mehmet's world right away. You feel his pain, his kindness, and his struggle to do the right thing. The bond between Mehmet and Ali is the heart of the story, and it keeps you watching even when things get heavy.

The acting is strong, especially the lead performance, which carries the whole film. The pacing is slow but steady, letting you sit with the characters and their emotions. On the downside, the story can feel a bit predictable at times, and some scenes drag. Still, if you enjoy emotional dramas with a twist, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you learn that Ali is not a real boy at all. He is a vision of Mehmet's younger self, born from years of childhood abuse and trauma. Mehmet has been talking to and caring for a version of himself he never got to protect. The twist reframes the whole movie as a story about a broken man finally facing his past. It ends on a bittersweet note as Mehmet begins to heal.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves emotional foreign dramas with a twist.
